mechanism_narrative: Grocery-pharmacy mobility has stabilized near baseline (-1.3% in t-0w) after declining from -8.0%, signaling reduced panic purchasing and normalization of essential-goods behavior. This normalization frees household budget and time allocation toward discretionary retail-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -8.0% to -1.3% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the prior 28-day mean, or GROCERY_PHARM reverts to decline below -5% in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has plateaued at +11.6% (t-0w), indicating stable lockdown compliance without further tightening. Sustained residential elevation without acceleration suggests behavioral adaptation is complete; retail-recreation will decline further as pent-up demand exhausts and risk aversion persists.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at +10.3% to +11.6% over three weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below +8% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points relative to the prior 28-day mean.

This week-on-week deterioration in commuting infrastructure use signals renewed mobility restrictions or behavioral retrenchment. Reduced transit access constrains retail-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 1.5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -29.0% to -31.4% in most recent week
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers to above -30% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points in the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Workplaces mobility collapsed from -27.7% (t-1w) to -35.4% (t-0w), a 7.7-point drop. This sharp deterioration indicates new workplace restrictions or lockdown intensification. candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -27.7% to -35.4% in most recent week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers to above -30% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 4 percentage points relative to the prior 28-day mean.

This behavioral regime will suppress retail-recreation mobility over the next four weeks as consumers remain cautious about indoor discretionary venues.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -50% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 6 percentage points relative to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Retail-recreation has shown consistent week-on-week improvement from -36.9% (t-3w) to -32.4% (t-0w), a 4.5-point gain over three weeks. This linear recovery trend, if sustained, will continue lifting retail-recreation mobility over the next four weeks as consumers gradually resume discretionary visits.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -36.9% to -32.4% over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in any of the next two weeks, or the four-week mean does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-pharmacy stabilization at -1.3% (t-0w) combined with workplace collapse to -35.4% creates a divergence: essential-goods access is normalizing while employment-linked mobility is deteriorating. This split signals that retail-recreation will remain suppressed because workplace-commuting-adjacent retail visits are eliminated, offsetting any gains from normalized grocery behavior.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -30% AND GROCERY_PHARM is above -5%
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers to above -30% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points in the next 14 days.

Transit mobility at -31.4% and workplace mobility at -35.4% indicate severe restrictions that override seasonal demand. Retail-recreation will decline further over the next four weeks as seasonal uplift is suppressed by mobility constraints, not enabled by them.
